title: Launch Readiness & Incident Review - Aurelia Health
summary: Internal launch-readiness sync combined with a post-incident review for the Dedicated pilot. Covered incident timeline, root-cause hypotheses (autoscaler edge case + KV cache invalidation), immediate mitigations, runbook gaps, and launch checklist items (KMS integration, SSO, SLAs). Owners and due dates assigned for postmortem, runbook updates, and pilot gating criteria. Action to share benchmark spreadsheet and updated runbook by 2026-11-10.
topics: Launch readiness checklist (security/compliance, KMS, SSO, monitoring)
Roadmap prioritization: autoscaler fixes, KV cache persistence, deterministic quantization testing

Schedule engineering deep-dive to reproduce autoscaler edge case (Priya + Mark)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood PM), Rita Patel (CTO, Aurelia), Mark Dawson (Infra Lead), Sofia Alvarez (Product), Tom Greer (Security)
Links referenced: internal runbook (link: https://redwood.link/runbook-aur-2026), benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.link/benchmarks-aur), pricing addendum (sent later)

Auto-summary (optional): We ran through the outage that impacted two Dedicated nodes during the pilot last week, discussed short-term mitigations and longer-term fixes, and aligned on launch gating criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jamie: Okay everyone we will kick off, thanks for joining. we have about 55 minutes, agenda is incident review, quick launch checklist and owners. Priya you want to start with the timeline?
[00:00:28] Priya: Yeah sure, so on 10/31 at 09:15 UTC we saw elevated error rates on two dedicated pools, the autoscaler attempted to rebalance and... uh, the node drain seemed to hang, there was a KV cash - sorry KV cache invalidation that caused replays. Some of the transcriptions in the logs say "KV cash" which made debugging confusing.
[00:00:52] Mark: Right, from our side the repro shows a spike in tail latencies, and we saw the drain process waiting on grpc streams, which is unusual. I captured logs and put them in the s3 bucket.
[00:01:15] Priya: Thanks Mark, that matches our traces, the redis-like cache eviction had a race with the prefix caching layer, so some requests attempted to replay with a stale cache key which increased load.
[00:01:40] Liam: Hypothesis then is autoscaler triggered concurrently with KV cache invalidation; the system couldn't gracefully warm the new host's KV state causing request failures. Does that align?
[00:01:55] Priya: Yeah that's the working hypothesis, we need a repro to be sure, possibly an ordering bug in the warmup handshake.
[00:02:10] Rita: For us the customer impact was primarily in the health triage flow, some users saw degraded responses for about 12 minutes, and then it auto-recovered. The business asks: what are the SLAs we can promise for the pilot?
[00:02:35] Jamie: Good question, Liam can you remind us of the current pilot SLA proposal?
[00:02:48] Liam: We're proposing a 99.5% availability for the pilot with 100ms p50 target for standard routes and a 2-second soft p95 for more complex generations; but we put in automatic fallback to a smaller model for critical paths to reduce impact. Need to validate those numbers against the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:03:12] Sofia: Is fallback to hosted allowed for the pilot? data residency is a constraint for us so we can't send some traffic off-prem.
[00:03:28] Jamie: Right, we discussed routing policies earlier — fallback can be regional or model-variant, not necessarily leaving the VPC if we're on Dedicated. But we need to confirm with security.
[00:03:45] Tom: From security/legal, we need KMS integration and audit log retention before we sign off on any fallback that leaves customer-managed keys. also SSO/SAML must be in place.
[00:04:04] Priya: Noted. For the technical fixes, short term we can pin the autoscaler to avoid concurrent drains, add additional health checks during warmup, and add a guarded KV cache invalidation path. Long term we want persistent KV snapshotting to avoid cold starts.
[00:04:30] Mark: Question about snapshotting: will that add storage overhead per model version? we need to model cost.
[00:04:44] Liam: Yes it will increase storage, but it reduces token cost by avoiding regen and reduces downtime. Priya do you have an estimate?
[00:04:58] Priya: Rough ballpark—initial estimate is 5-10 GB per active shard depending on KV size, we should quantify after we repro.
[00:05:18] Jamie: Okay, let's go through the runbook gaps. Priya what was missing that made the incident harder to mitigate?
[00:05:32] Priya: Two main things: first the runbook didn't include explicit steps for concurrent autoscaler drains, and second there wasn't a clear rollback to previous model variant in the Dedicated pool when warmup fails. also our logging didn't tag the model variant consistently which slowed traceability.
[00:05:56] Jamie: Good, we'll add those items. Action: Priya will draft postmortem and runbook updates.
[00:06:10] Sofia: On the launch checklist we need to ensure KMS+HSM support is documented, plus an audit retention policy that meets Aurelia's compliance. Rita any specific retention numbers?
[00:06:26] Rita: We need seven years for certain audit logs for the healthcare workflows, but we might scope to just request-level metadata for that retention. More from legal on exact fields.
[00:06:44] Tom: Yep, Tom will confirm the exact KMS posture and retention fields, I'll follow up.
[00:06:55] Jamie: On the pilot gating criteria, Liam can you outline the must-haves?
[00:07:06] Liam: Sure: 1) KMS and audit logs in place, 2) runbook updates and at least one successful chaos/repro test of the autoscaler, 3) agreed SLAs and fallback behavior documented, 4) performance benchmarks matching p50/p95 targets under the expected workload.
[00:07:36] Rita: For the perf benchmarks, who will run those? We can run an internal load and share traces.
[00:07:46] Mark: I'll run the internal load repro and share the logs and traces, noted in action items.
[00:07:58] Priya: We'll coordinate with Mark to reproduce the race and then test the autoscaler guard. If repro is stable, we'll try the snapshotting prototype.
[00:08:12] Jamie: There was also an ask from product about the UX during incidents, we should surface clearer error messages and degrade gracefully, not just timeouts.
[00:08:26] Sofia: Agreed — product wants a customer-facing doc for expected failure modes and mitigation steps to present to support.
[00:08:38] Jamie: We'll provide that as part of the launch pack.
[00:08:45] Priya: Also note that metrics on the tracer were missing a correlation id for some of the failed requests, that's a telemetry gap.
[00:08:58] Liam: Add correlation id to request path instrumentation, that's a small change but high value.
[00:09:12] Priya: I'll add it to the runbook updates.
[00:09:18] Jamie: On the SLA/pricing side, I'll send the pricing addendum to Rita after this call and include the benchmark spreadsheet; action assigned.
[00:09:31] Rita: Thanks Jamie, we'll review and get back with any objections.
[00:09:40] Tom: Security question — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS per-host in Dedicated or is it per-tenant? we need to know for our legal doc.
[00:09:55] Priya: Today we support customer-managed keys at the tenant level for encryption at rest; per-host HSM is on the roadmap but not available in pilot. We'll note that as a constraint.
[00:10:12] Tom: That's helpful. We'll need a signed exception if we can't get per-host HSM for certain regulated workloads.
[00:10:23] Jamie: We'll capture that in the legal follow-up item.
[00:10:29] Priya: Another action: add stronger health checks during warmup and a timeout backoff so drains don't overlap.
[00:10:39] Mark: Also consider a draining isolation window to prevent multiple nodes draining for the same shard simultaneously.
[00:10:49] Liam: Good call, that could be a short-term policy change in the autoscaler config.
[00:10:59] Jamie: Ok let's fast-forward to roadmap implications: is this a quick fix or do we need more engineering cycles?
[00:11:10] Priya: Short term: config and runbook changes ~2-3 engineer-days. Medium term: snapshotting + deterministic warmup testing is an engineering project—estimate 3 sprints to build and validate.
[00:11:28] Liam: We should prioritize snapshotting higher because it benefits many customers and reduces cost by avoiding re-generation.
[00:11:36] Jamie: Agree, let's aim to schedule the snapshotting spike next sprint.
[00:11:42] Sofia: Does snapshotting affect quantization profiles or kernel selection? we rely on deterministic kernels for low-latency.
[00:11:53] Priya: It shouldn't change kernel selection, but we'd need to ensure KV format is compatible across quantization profiles; that's part of the validation matrix.
[00:12:06] Jamie: Noted.
[00:12:12] Jamie: Any blockers from customer side for launch?
[00:12:18] Rita: The main blockers are KMS confirmation and SLA signoff; plus we want a rehearsal of incident playbook.
[00:12:29] Tom: Legal will need to review the exceptions and retention table, I'll target 2026-11-12 to confirm.
[00:12:40] Jamie: Great. We'll now record the owner assignments - going once.
[00:12:45] Priya: I'll put together the postmortem doc, include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and runbook changes.
[00:12:55] Jamie: Liam will update the launch checklist and gating criteria.
[00:13:02] Liam: Yes, I'll produce an updated checklist and circulate with acceptance criteria.
[00:13:08] Mark: I'll run the load repro and share traces and logs in the s3 bucket.
[00:13:14] Jamie: Tom will confirm KMS/legal.
[00:13:18] Tom: Correct.
[00:13:21] Jamie: Okay before we close any other questions?
[00:13:25] Sofia: Quick one — are we committed to providing a canary rollback plan for the pilot?
[00:13:33] Jamie: Yes, canary and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant is part of the plan but we need to document exact routing rules.
[00:13:43] Priya: One last note, the telemetry team flagged that traces were sampled too low during the incident, we should bump sample rate for Dedicated pilot for the next two weeks.
[00:13:56] Liam: We'll temporarily increase sampling and then revert after pilot.
[00:14:02] Jamie: Great, thanks everyone. I'll send the notes and the pricing addendum. Priya will share the postmortem link when ready. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts: occasional misheard words (e.g., "KV cash"), timestamps approximate, speaker overlaps occasionally labeled generically.
